svg.title: How the standalone runtime runs the same integration code without Home Assistant
svg.desc: One integration package in the middle, two runtimes above it. Home Assistant imports the real homeassistant package; the standalone runtime puts a shim at the front of sys.path so that the same import resolves to it. Below the integration, the gateway and the hardware are identical in both cases.
svg.text: The standalone runtime — not a second implementation
Both columns load the very same custom_components/eltako. Only what `import homeassistant` resolves to is different.
Home Assistant
runs the house · starts in tens of seconds
import homeassistant
the real package
brings everything a home automation system has:
automations, scenes, history, other integrations
eltako_standalone
test, analyse, calibrate · starts in about a second
import homeassistant
resolves to hass_shim/ — put first on sys.path
runtime.py boots it · server.py serves http + ws
entity_api.py holds the states · cli.py is the CLI
custom_components/eltako — unchanged
The same async_setup / async_setup_entry, the same gateways, entities, catalog, observers, web ui and websocket api.
core/ config/ catalog/ observation/ simulation/ tools/ frontend/
EnOceanGateway → serial port, USB stick or LAN gateway → the real bus and the real radio
On macOS and Windows the standalone runtime reaches a USB gateway natively, which a docker container cannot.
The shim replaces the real homeassistant package, so the two test suites must not share a pytest process — it poisons the other suite’s imports.
